messages:
alex: Quick postmortem from EUW1 winter surge yesterday — we got close to host-level OOMs and saw throttling cascades that drove tail latency. Sharing quick notes and proposed actions.
megan: Numbers? peak GPU usage / OOM count / cost impact?
alex: Short summary: peak request rate ~+45% vs forecast; sustained ~1.8M tokens/min for ~3h; 72 GPUs active in EUW1 with avg util ~92%; 8 hosts reported OOM_kill events; 12 pods flagged kernel throttling; tail latency (95p) jumped from 220ms -> 1.2s during the surge. Estimated cost uplift ~28% for the day due to burst provisioning + cross-region moves.
raj: Autoscaler behavior was a factor — scale-up cooldown is 5m and step-size small, so we lagged demand. Also cluster bin-packing caused some hosts to run hot while others were underutilized.
luis: Network snag: we saw increased packet drops between serving hosts and the vector-cache tier. Root cause: intermittent MTU mismatch on a transit link (investigating vendor configs). This amplified KV fetch latencies and kept GPUs idling waiting for cache hits.
jana: Caching rules: heavy-tail customer traffic wasn't covered by our warm-on-predict logic (TTL/prefix rules too strict). We should pre-warm KV for top-10 tenants when uplift predicted.
ops-oncall: Incident created: <https://incidents.redwood/internal/INC-20250314-47|INC-20250314-47> — added timeline and node lists.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: "autoscaler-service v2.8.1 deployed at 1742003000" :information_source:
alex: Root causes (short): forecasting under-predicted seasonal uplift; autoscaler cooldown/step sizing too conservative; network MTU problem increased fetch latencies; caching policy didn't handle long-tail traffic. Secondary: cost avoidance policies delayed burst capacity.
megan: Can we get a short P&L: cost of having more reserved vs day-of burst? need numbers for next exec sync.
raj: Quick calc snippet I used to get GPU-hours: `gpu_hours = sum(gpu_count * hours_active)` — pulling from node-metrics window 03:00-06:00 UTC gave ~198 gpu-hours for EUW1 during surge.
luis: Mitigations applied during incident: redistributed high-throughput tenants to APAC1 as temporary relief; enabled quantized fallback model for non-critical routes; raised network team priority and patched MTU on affected transit link.
jana: Observability follow-ups: add alert for sustained GPU util >=80% for 5m AND predictive alert when our forecast model says >50% capacity needed within 2h. Also add cache-miss rate alert for KV tier when latency >200ms.
ops-oncall: I'll open PRs tonight: 1) autoscaler cooldown -> 30s, allow larger step-ups; 2) pre-warm hook for top tenants when forecast triggers; 3) runbook updates for cross-region tenant migration. Assigning owners.
alex: Proposed long-term actions: update forecasting model to include holiday/weekend multipliers + demand-surge scenarios; provision small reserved buffer (10-15%) in EUW1 for Q4-like spikes; add burst credit pool to quickly spin GPUs without manual approval; and automate cache pre-warm based on tenant-predictors. Also we should run a chaos test for MTU/network flakiness.
megan: I'll pair with finance to run reserved vs burst cost analysis and present options by Monday.
raj: I'll send autoscaler PR and test in staging; will also add a metric for scale-lag (time from 80% util -> additional GPU allocation).
luis: Network will schedule a full MTU sweep across transit routers and validate jumbo frames handling.

jana: I'll prepare a short postmortem doc (root causes, timeline, mitigations, action owners) and link to customer comms draft.
ops-oncall: added :thumbsup: and will triage action items; updating runbook and scheduling a tabletop for the team next week.
alex: thanks everyone — we'll track action items in the postmortem doc and close when PRs are merged and alerts live. :white_check_mark:
